title: A Crushing Victory
next_chapter_hook: Just as the crowd hadn't recovered from their shock, the turtle shell in his arms burned hot once more, and a force that had been dormant for ages was about to break free from its shell...

text.content: When the morning bell rang its seventh toll, the Tianqing Sect Martial Arena was already packed with people. Today was the first day of the Sect Competition. Sunlight pierced through the thin mist, casting golden rays across the vast arena platform. Yet the murmurs from the crowd drowned out the wind—"Did you hear? That waste of a servant actually signed up!" "Hahaha, isn't this just sending himself to his death?" "Han Lie's confidant Zhao Hu is at Foundation Building Seventh Stage, one punch could break three stone pillars!" Chen Ji stood at the very end of the competitor's line, his expression calm as still water, only the turtle shell in his arms burning so hot it almost seared. It was as if a caged beast was stirring restlessly within.

dialogue.content: Hahaha! Chen Ji, you actually dare to come?

text.content: Han Lie strode forward, his confidant Zhao Hu trailing behind. That face crisscrossed with knife scars was filled with contempt. Chen Ji glanced at the two men, the corner of his lips curving slightly, yet he said nothing. This "timid" appearance, in Han Lie's eyes, only made him laugh even more wildly. "Later, let Zhao Hu teach you some proper manners! Don't think you can act high and mighty just because you latched onto Sister Su—my man, Han Lie—" Before he could finish, the copper gong suddenly sounded, announcing the first round matchups.

dialogue.content: First match—Servant Disciple Chen Ji versus Xuanwu Sect's Zhao Hu!

text.content: The entire arena erupted. Zhao Hu burst into laughter, flipping Chen Ji the middle finger: "Kid, it's not too late to surrender, otherwise later—" He made a throat-slitting gesture. Laughter erupted all around; no one gave that waste a chance. Chen Ji walked slowly toward the center of the arena platform, his robes fluttering gently in the morning breeze. The turtle shell in his arms grew increasingly scalding, that power almost breaking through its constraints. He lowered his gaze and silently recited: Tianji Record, just give me three breaths.

At the referee's command, Zhao Hu launched his attack with murderous force! His right fist gathered earth-yellow spiritual light—that was the Xuanwu Sect's exclusive "Mountain Suppression Fist," a single strike carrying ten thousand jin of force. Shouts rose from below—"This waste is finished!" Yet Chen Ji merely sidestepped, and that seemingly clumsy iron fist whistled past his sleeve. Zhao Hu's pupils constricted sharply, before he could change his technique, a sharp sword intent had already pressed against his throat. "You—when did you—?!"

Silence fell over the entire arena. No one saw Chen Ji draw his sword—one cold flash of light, and Zhao Hu's fist froze mid-air, while that ordinary iron sword already rested against his neck. Chen Ji looked down at that face twisted with fear, and suddenly spoke softly: "What rules was Brother Zhao saying he'd teach me just now?" His voice wasn't loud, yet it clearly reached everyone's ears. "Now, it's my turn to teach you." The blade turned, spiritual energy erupted!

Chen Ji's wrist flicked, and Zhao Hu was swept up by a gentle force, flipping three times in the air before crashing heavily at the arena platform's edge. The impact shattered the stone tiles. Zhao Hu spat blood, struggling but unable to rise. One move. Just one move, and Foundation Building Seventh Stage Zhao Hu was utterly defeated. The whole arena erupted into chaos, discussion surging like a tide—"This...is this still that waste?" "When did he become so powerful?" Chen Ji sheathed his sword, his expression indifferent, as if he'd merely done something insignificant.

Chen Ji turned around, his gaze passing through the crowd, landing precisely on Han Lie's ashen face. He smiled faintly—that smile was gentle and harmless, yet in Han Lie's eyes it was a hundred times more irritating than any mockery. "Brother Han Lie," Chen Ji called out, his voice clear and bright, "your sect's confidant doesn't seem to be all that impressive." At these words, the entire arena exploded. The Xuanwu Sect disciples' expressions turned ugly, while quite a few Tianqing Sect disciples secretly cheered—this waste who'd been bullied so badly every day had finally gotten some revenge!

dialogue.content: You wait! In the next match I'll personally—

text.content: Before Han Lie could finish, a sharp gaze pressed down upon him. Su Qingyao had appeared at the arena's edge at some unknown moment. Her icy gaze swept over him as she coldly said: "Sect Competition forbids private combat. Han Lie, you're the Xuanwu Sect's Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, not a street thug." Han Lie's face cycled through green and white, yet he dared not defy the Inner Sect's top disciple. He could only clench his teeth and retreat. Su Qingyao turned to Chen Ji, her gaze complex and unfathomable. This waste...when did he gain such strength? Her intuition told her this person was far from being as simple as he appeared.

On the high platform, Ling Yuan's gaze pierced through the crowd, falling upon Chen Ji. The old sect master narrowed his eyes, his fingertips tapping lightly on the armrest. This lad chosen by the Tianji Record was more troublesome than he'd imagined. Was he blinded by the Tianji Record's power, or was he deliberately feigning weakness? Alarm bells rang in his heart, yet on the surface he merely stroked his beard and smiled, as if appreciating an entertaining performance. Below, Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul trembled slightly within Chen Ji's embrace. The turtle shell's temperature had shifted from scalding to merely warm—some power was awakening.

The competition continued. Chen Ji won match after match, each victory a clean, decisive crushing. Servant disciple? Waste? These labels shattered into jokes before the ironclad facts. The audience's attitude shifted from mockery to shock, then from shock to reverence. As the final match concluded, Chen Ji stood with his sword sheathed. The setting sun stretched his shadow long. "This kid..." an elder murmured, "is likely about to soar to great heights." Yet Chen Ji merely lowered his eyes slightly, feeling that strange pulse from the turtle shell in his arms—the omen of some power about to break free from its shell.

As the crowd gradually dispersed, Su Qingyao walked up to Chen Ji, blocking his path. She examined this former waste with scrutinizing eyes, curiosity flickering within them. "You've hidden yourself very deeply." She spoke bluntly, "From today onward, you're no longer a servant disciple." She raised her hand, and a token flew toward Chen Ji—the identity credential of an Inner Disciple. Chen Ji accepted the token, his expression unchanged: "Many thanks, Sister Su." Su Qingyao stared into his eyes, seemingly trying to discern something, yet she only saw a calm lake.

At this moment, the turtle shell in his embrace shuddered violently once more. Chen Ji's expression shifted slightly as he calmly pressed his hand against his chest. Su Qingyao noticed his unusual state, frowning faintly: "What's wrong?" Chen Ji shook his head, forcing a smile: "Nothing, just the earlier match drained me too much. I feel a bit unwell." Su Qingyao clearly didn't believe him, yet she didn't press further, only saying coldly: "There are far too many suspicious points about you. Someday, I will investigate them all." With that, she turned and left. Chen Ji gazed at her departing figure, the corner of his lips curving into a meaningful arc.

Night deepened. Chen Ji returned to his modest dwelling. The moment he closed the door, he finally pressed his hand against his chest and let out a muffled groan. The turtle shell had reached a terrifying temperature. That force rampaged through his body, as if wanting to tear through flesh and bone. He sat cross-legged, attempting to suppress it, yet to no avail. Countless fine cracks spread across the turtle shell's surface, golden light seeping through the fissures. "This is..." Chen Ji's pupils dilated sharply, "the second page?!" Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his mind: "The Tianji Record recognized its master long ago. The first page's power you've already mastered. Now, the second page's fortuitous encounter...has arrived."
